findings.trigger: clean_sweep_bot_messages (or any non-purge cleanup) finds N bot messages; the bulk delete fails with discord.HTTPException (e.g. a Discord 5xx after the library's own retries, or a 400 for a message that turned out too old), so _bulk_delete_messages falls back to _individual_delete_messages, where every message.delete() raises HTTPException too -> each failure is logged only at DEBUG (line 390) and counted nowhere. In cleanup_channel, success is computed at line 241 as `permission_errors == 0 and timeout_errors == 0`, both still 0 -> result.success = True, result.error = None, log says '✅ CLEANUP SUCCESS: Deleted 0/N messages'. The same happens directly for messages older than 14 days, which always take the individual path. A cleanup that deleted nothing is reported as done (Z3), and the cause is only in the debug log (Z8). The A11 comment above line 241 claims 'Success only if nothing was refused' but only two of the failure kinds are counted.
findings.suggestion: Count the generic delete failures in _individual_delete_messages (e.g. result.other_errors += 1, or compare messages_deleted with messages_found) and let cleanup_channel set success = False with an error text when messages_deleted < messages_found; log the per-message failure at WARNING, not DEBUG.

findings.trigger: The bot has no 'Manage Messages' in a channel. (a) delete_bot_messages_preserve_live_logs: channel.purge() raises Forbidden -> permission_errors += 1 (line 428) -> _delete_one_by_one deletes every one of the bot's own messages (which needs no permission, as the D33 comment right above says) -> back in cleanup_channel line 241 permission_errors is 1 -> result.success = False, result.error = '1 message(s) could not be deleted - the bot is missing the permission in this channel', although messages_deleted == messages_found; then line 270 still logs '✅ CLEANUP SUCCESS'. (b) The same for clean_sweep_bot_messages with >= 2 recent messages: channel.delete_messages raises Forbidden -> permission_errors += 1 (line 359) -> the individual fallback deletes all -> reported as failed for a missing permission. (c) When the purge-Forbidden fallback deletes only the capped 50 of, say, 120 found, the shortfall is attributed to a permission the operator does not need to grant, not to the 50-message cap. The D33 comment (the refusal 'says nothing about the work itself') and the A11 success rule contradict each other in code: the shortcut's refusal is counted exactly like a refused message.
findings.suggestion: Do not count the refused bulk/purge shortcut in permission_errors (count only per-message Forbidden in the fallbacks), or track it separately (shortcut_refused) and exclude it from the success rule; for the 50-cap case set an error naming the cap (as the timeout branch already does). Also emit the 'CLEANUP SUCCESS' log only when result.success is True.

findings.trigger: delete_bot_messages_preserve_live_logs on a channel whose last 200 messages contain bot messages older than max_age_days (30). _collect_messages skips them (line 295-296) and does not count them in messages_found; if at least one younger bot message exists, cleanup proceeds to channel.purge(limit=200, check=filter), whose check is the custom filter alone - no age cutoff - so the old messages are deleted anyway and purge_deleted can exceed messages_found ('Deleted 15 messages', found 10). If NO bot message is younger than 30 days, the early return at line 218-222 deletes nothing and reports success. The max_age_days threshold is honoured on one path and silently ignored on the other, and the two paths give different results for the same channel.
findings.suggestion: Either pass `after=cutoff_date` to channel.purge() (or wrap the check with the age test) so the purge respects max_age_days, or, if the intent is 'all bot messages', drop the age filter for this request so both branches agree.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the 30-day default is meant to apply to this method at all, and py-cord's purge() handling of messages older than 14 days (I recall it switches to single deletes), are not visible here.

findings.trigger: An installation with more than 50 tracked messages (channel:display_name keys), e.g. 60 containers in one status channel, all of them updated on every beat. Whenever an update_content call lands exactly on total_ops % 100 == 0, _cleanup_cache keeps 25 entries and drops the other 35 LIVE keys. On the next beat has_content_changed returns True for each of those 35 ('first time seeing this key') although their content is unchanged -> 35 unnecessary Discord edits, repeated roughly every 100 operations. The service exists to avoid exactly these API calls, and the D34 fix (recency order) does not help when the working set itself is larger than keep_entries.
findings.suggestion: Size the cache by the working set (e.g. keep_entries = max(25, number of keys seen in the last N beats)) or evict only entries not touched for a fixed time instead of a fixed count.

findings.trigger: The operator has given the DDC container a StopTimeout (e.g. 60 s so a running scheduled task or a pending write can finish) and presses the panel's restart button. _do_it calls containers.get(id).restart() with no timeout, so docker-py sends its default timeout=10 and Docker SIGKILLs DDC after 10 s regardless of the configured StopTimeout. get_stop_timeout_kwargs in docker_action_service.py exists precisely to avoid this for every other container; DDC's own restart is the one place that does not use it (two places doing the same thing, drifting).
findings.suggestion: Call .restart(**get_stop_timeout_kwargs(container)) (import inside _do_it to avoid a module-level cycle), or at least pass the container's StopTimeout explicitly.

findings.trigger: note_own_action(name, action) is recorded at line 189 before the action; it is withdrawn (forget) only for docker.errors.APIError. If the daemon connection drops between containers.get and the action, action_func raises requests.ConnectionError (an OSError) -> nothing happened in Docker, the outer except returns success=False, but the own-action note stays. If somebody else stops that container while the note is still remembered, the watchdog treats the stop as DDC's own and neither alarms nor restarts. The comment at 182-187 justifies keeping the note only for the read-timeout case ('Docker carries it out'), not for a connection that never delivered the request.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a read timeout (keep the note) from a connection error (forget the note), e.g. `except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: forget(...); raise` before the OSError handling, or forget on any non-timeout failure.
findings.unsure_why: services/automation/own_actions.py is not in this section: how long a note lives and what exactly the watchdog does with it decide whether the window matters.

findings.trigger: A group 'Gameserver' allows 'stop'; one of its member containers has allowed_actions without 'stop' (the operator deliberately protected that one container). A stop on 'group:Gameserver' passes the group's allowed_actions check at line 112 and then calls docker_action_service_first(member, 'stop') for every member, which checks no per-container allowed_actions anywhere in this section -> the protected container is stopped. Z5 demands 'the container allows the action' on every path, and B2 says 'which actions are allowed stays with the container's own allowed_actions'.
findings.suggestion: If the operator's 2026-09-24 decision really means the group's list replaces the members' lists, record that in SPEC.md as a deliberate decision; otherwise skip (and name in the outcome, like `missing`) every member whose own allowed_actions does not contain the action.
findings.unsure_why: services/config/group_service.members_of and the callers are not visible; members_of may already filter, or the callers may check each member beforehand. The module docstring ('THE GROUP DECIDES') reads as if this is intended, but SPEC.md does not record it.

findings.trigger: clean_sweep_bot_messages called with message_limit > 100 (default is 100) in a channel with more than 100 bot messages younger than 14 days -> channel.delete_messages(messages) is handed more than 100 messages; discord.py/py-cord raise discord.ClientException (not an HTTPException, not a RuntimeError), which neither the except clauses at 357-366 nor cleanup_channel's at 273 catch -> the exception escapes cleanup_channel to the caller with no ChannelCleanupResult; execution_time is set in finally, but nothing was deleted and nothing says so in the result.
findings.suggestion: Chunk bulk_eligible into slices of at most 100 before delete_messages, or add discord.ClientException to the fallback clause at line 363.
findings.unsure_why: No caller in this section passes a message_limit above 100; whether any caller elsewhere does is not visible.

notes: Section overall: the four Discord services are decision/caching layers, the Docker files are the only ones that touch containers, and both keep to start/stop/restart (Z6 holds here, self_restart uses only restart). F1 also applies to cleanup_channel and F8 to clean_sweep_bot_messages; one finding id per verdict was kept. Not findings, recorded so they are not lost: (1) channel_cleanup_service.py:413-417 - when the purge times out, the messages purge already deleted are not counted (purge_deleted stays 0), so the 'X of N were deleted' error under-reports; harmless because it is reported as incomplete anyway. (2) channel_cleanup_service.py:144 - keep_message_ids is compared with message.id (int); a caller passing string ids would keep nothing, callers not visible. (3) conditional_update_cache_service.py:94 stores the caller's dict by reference; a caller that mutates it afterwards corrupts the comparison - callers not visible. (4) status_overview_service.py:306 - 'config_source' is always 'cached' because _get_channel_update_config has just filled the cache; debug output only. (5) status_overview_service.py:122-128 - with enable_auto_refresh False, force_recreate (a mech level change) is also refused; reads as intended ('disabled means do not touch') but is not written down. (6) status_overview_service.py:285 - the except lists discord errors for pure dict parsing; a non-int update_interval_minutes (e.g. a string from a form) becomes a TypeError in timedelta at line 137, caught by the broad clause at 169 -> 'always update' with an ERROR log every beat; whether the writer stores ints is not visible. (7) should_update_channel_overview passes no beat_seconds (grace 5 s) while the status loop path does; two callers of is_due may drift - callers not visible. (8) group_actions.py:104 catches only OSError around the group read; a corrupt groups file (JSONDecodeError is a ValueError) would escape act_on_group loudly unless group_service catches it - not visible. (9) group_actions.py:128 - a wait_for timeout cancels the awaiting task while the to_thread call and the Docker stop continue; the async client context exit is cancelled too - whether the pool recovers that client is not visible. (10) docker_action_service.py:240 - on Python 3.10 (CI) asyncio.TimeoutError is not an OSError; whether get_docker_client_async can raise it is not visible. (11) _delete_one_by_one's `elif not request.custom_filter` branch is unreachable in practice (only called with a custom filter).
